title: Distributed Saturation Matrix for TP/PP throughput & latency regression detection
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Build a reproducible distributed saturation matrix that exercises combinations of tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) partitions across heterogeneous multi-GPU clusters and automatically detects regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency. This harness will become the canonical nightly stress/regression feed for inference CI and populate dashboards used by SRE and the runtime team.

Scope:
- Sweep TP x PP configurations (e.g., TP 1..8, PP 1..8) across supported model families (small/med/large) and quantization profiles.
- Measure steady-state tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and variance over 15m sustained windows.
- Add microburst subtests (short 30s high-concurrency bursts) and KV-cache warm/cold modes.
- Produce a saturation matrix visual (heatmap) linking config -> achieved throughput and p95.
- Implement regression detection: baseline control charts + EWMA anomaly detector with configurable sensitivity, and a bootstrap-backed significance test for flagged regressions.
- Integrate results into Grafana (runtime-performance board), upload raw artifacts to GCS, and file a PR with the summary report on every nightly run.

Methodology & design decisions:
- Use stable synthetic workload: deterministic prompt templates, token lengths sampled from production distribution.
- Warmup: 3 full-length warmup runs per config to populate KV cache and JIT kernels; discard warmup from metrics.
- Steady-state windows: run for 15 minutes per config, compute metrics over the last 10 minutes; for long-running configs (>1 hour) segment into 10-minute windows to detect drift.
- Regression thresholds: start with 7% tokens/sec drop or 15% p95 increase vs. baseline for an automatic alert; thresholds are adjustable and will be tuned during initial rollout.
- Noise handling: run each cell 3 independent trials and report median; use ANOVA to estimate if variance exceeds acceptable bounds.

Telemetry & observability:
- Expose per-token breakdown: kernel launch times, memcpy, cross-node latency, scheduling wait time.
- Tag runs with node image, driver, CUDA/CUDNN versions, and model artifact SHA for reproducibility.
- Dashboard will surface per-config health, historical trend, and regression alerts with links to raw logs and profiling flamegraphs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can complete full TPxPP sweep for medium model in <= 12 hours on our CI fleet or run distributedly across pool nodes with orchestration.
- Nightly job publishes JSON artifacts, Grafana panels update, and regression detection opens ENG tickets when thresholds are exceeded.
- Minimal flakiness: median of repeated runs must have coefficient of variation < 8% for tokens/sec in steady-state.

Risks & mitigations:
- Heterogeneous hardware causes noisy signals: mitigate by grouping results by instance class and normalizing to microarchitecture baseline.
- Orchestration failures at scale: fallback to smaller parallelism per-run and shard matrix across multiple CI jobs.
- Long runtime cost: enable partial sweeps and prioritized cells based on past sensitivity and customer usage patterns.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Distributed+Saturation+Matrix
- Spike PR with prototype harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1891
- Example Grafana board (draft): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt-saturation/throughput-matrix
